recommendations.regimenLabel: Diagnostic tap + treat cause; drain if symptomatic/infected
steps: Diagnostic pleural aspiration (US-guided) — protein, LDH, pH, cytology, microbiology.
Apply Light's criteria; treat the underlying cause (heart failure, malignancy, etc.).
Therapeutic drainage for breathlessness (avoid >1.5 L at once — re-expansion oedema).
Malignant effusion: consider indwelling pleural catheter or pleurodesis.

drugRefs.dose: 4–5 g slurry via chest drain (or 2–5 g poudrage at thoracoscopy)
drugRefs.freq: single instillation after full lung re-expansion
drugRefs.why: Standard sclerosant to obliterate the pleural space and prevent re-accumulation in recurrent malignant effusion; an alternative to an indwelling pleural catheter.

refs: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Disorders of the Pleura

decision.label: Diagnostic tap; drain if symptomatic or infected

confirm: Dyspnoea with stony dull base, reduced breath sounds; CXR/US confirms. Tap to classify (Light's criteria: exudate vs transudate).
